# Cross-project leak markers
#
# One regex per line. Patterns matched here trigger a Phase 5.3.5 leak-scan
# failure during /setup-project. The scan walks every generated rule / agent /
# pattern / convention file looking for these markers, on the assumption that
# they would only appear if the LLM accidentally carried content from a
# different project's setup.
#
# When to add a regex here:
#  - You found a generated file in project B that referenced project A's
#    internal codename, base class, or business term.
#  - You have an internal product name that should NEVER appear in a
#    shareable artifact (rules, packs, adapters).
#
# When NOT to add:
#  - Generic framework / language names (NestJS, Django, Postgres, etc.) —
#    those are detected from the actual stack and verified separately.
#  - Open-source library names — same.
#
# Format: a POSIX-extended regex (passed to `grep -E`). Comments start with #.
# Empty lines ignored. Patterns are case-insensitive when written with
# explicit alternations (e.g. `(Foo|FOO|foo)` if you need that).
#
# Example (commented out — uncomment + adapt for your own internal codenames):
#
# (?i)\binternal-codename-1\b
# (?i)\binternal-codename-2\b
#
# Default: no markers. The scan still validates extraction-traceability +
# stack-match (Checks 1 + 2 in Phase 5.3.5); markers (Check 3) only fire when
# this file is populated.
